record.paper_title: Analysis on Faddeev Knots and Skyrme Solitons: Recent Progress and Open Problems
record.original_question: For the Faddeev minimization problem on bounded balls BR with constant boundary data and fixed Hopf charge N, let E^R_N be the minimum energy over maps BR → S^2 with Q(n)=N. As the radius R tends to infinity, does E^R_N converge to the full-space minimum EN? Equivalently, do minimizers on large bounded balls recover the full-space minimization problem in the limit?

evidence.quote: Energy splitting. For both Faddeev and Skyrme models, the existence of minimizers in every topological class of maps can be easily proved over a bounded contractible smooth domain in R3 (in particular, on a ball of radius R, say BR). Understanding of these minimizers as R → ∞ remains to be a difficult question. In fact, it is even unknown whether the minimum value (6.18) E^R_N = inf{E(n) | n : BR → S2, n|∂BR = const, Q(n) = N} satisfies E^R_N → EN as R → ∞.

artifact.self_contained_problem:
Let $S^2 \subset \mathbb{R}^3$ denote the standard unit 2-sphere. For a sufficiently smooth map $\mathbf{n}:\mathbb{R}^3 \to S^2$ that approaches a constant vector at infinity, define the Faddeev energy
$$E(\mathbf{n}) = \int_{\mathbb{R}^3} \Bigl(|\nabla \mathbf{n}|^2 + \tfrac{1}{2}\sum_{i,j=1}^{3} |\partial_i \mathbf{n} \wedge \partial_j \mathbf{n}|^2\Bigr)\,dx,$$
where $\mathbf{a}\wedge\mathbf{b}$ denotes the cross product in $\mathbb{R}^3$. Such a map extends continuously to $S^3 \to S^2$ and therefore has a Hopf invariant $Q(\mathbf{n}) \in \mathbb{Z}$. For each integer $N$, let
$$E_N = \inf\{E(\mathbf{n}) : \mathbf{n}:\mathbb{R}^3 \to S^2,\ Q(\mathbf{n}) = N\}.$$
For $R > 0$ let $B_R = \{x \in \mathbb{R}^3 : |x| < R\}$ and define
$$E^R_N = \inf\{E(\mathbf{n}) : \mathbf{n}:B_R \to S^2,\ \mathbf{n}|_{\partial B_R} = \text{const},\ Q(\mathbf{n}) = N\},$$
where $Q(\mathbf{n})$ is the Hopf charge of the extension obtained by collapsing $\partial B_R$ to a point (so the domain becomes $S^3$).

Question: Does $E^R_N \to E_N$ as $R \to \infty$? Equivalently, do the minimizers of the Faddeev energy on bounded balls with constant boundary data and prescribed Hopf charge $N$ recover, in the large-ball limit, the infimum of the full-space Faddeev minimization problem in the same topological class?
artifact.status_search_result: A web search yielded no result establishing or disproving the convergence $E^R_N \to E_N$ as $R\to\infty$ for the Faddeev minimization problem on balls with constant boundary data and fixed Hopf charge. Recent literature on the Faddeev model in bounded domains discusses existence of minimizers and the sublinear/fractional growth law $E_N \sim |N|^{3/4}$, but does not appear to resolve this large-ball limit question, which remains stated as an open problem in the available surveys.

status_evidence.title: Existence of Energy Minimizers as Stable Knotted Solitons in the Faddeev Model
status_evidence.snippet: Minimizers in each Hopf class exist in full space under the sublinear energy-charge inequality, but no statement on the large-ball limit of bounded-domain minimizers.
status_evidence.claim: Existence of full-space minimizers is established but the bounded-ball limit is not addressed.

status_evidence.title: Universal growth law for knot energy of Faddeev type in general dimensions
status_evidence.snippet: E_N satisfies a universal fractional-exponent growth law in |N| determined by the domain/range dimensions.
status_evidence.claim: Growth law for E_N is known but does not settle the convergence E^R_N → E_N.

status_evidence.title: Global minimality of the Hopf map in the Faddeev-Skyrme model with large coupling constant
status_evidence.snippet: Recent work on global minimality of the Hopf map in a Faddeev-Skyrme variant; does not address the large-ball convergence question.
status_evidence.claim: Recent related results do not resolve the large-ball convergence problem.
